title: Elasticsearch Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Elasticsearch course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: Which part is the document id?
exercises.explanation: An index is a group of searchable documents. A document has named fields, such as title and page count.

exercises.question: Which mapping suits an exact category name?
exercises.explanation: A mapping tells Elasticsearch how a field should be searched. text is for analysed words, while keyword is for exact values.

exercises.question: What does refresh visibility affect?
options: When search can see the new document
Whether the title is stored as a password
exercises.explanation: Indexing stores a document so search can use its fields. A refresh makes recently indexed data visible to search.

exercises.question: What is used to choose the document here?
exercises.explanation: The document get API reads a specific id. It is different from searching for words across many documents.

exercises.question: Which query is suited to analysed title words?
options: A term query on every text field blindly
exercises.explanation: A match query searches text using the field's analyser. It is suited to human words in a text field.

exercises.question: Why use keyword for kind?
options: It supports an exact category value
exercises.explanation: A term filter checks an exact indexed value. A keyword field is useful when category spelling should match exactly.

exercises.question: Does a 60-page book fit the range 30 through 80?
exercises.explanation: A range query selects numbers between bounds. gte means greater than or equal to, and lte means less than or equal to.

exercises.question: What must a returned document satisfy?
options: Both the title search and category filter
exercises.explanation: A bool query can combine word search with exact conditions. The word search can score relevance while filters restrict the allowed set.

exercises.question: What does _source selection limit?
exercises.explanation: A search request can limit its hit count and sort by a field. Source filtering returns only the fields the page needs.

exercises.question: What does each bucket count represent?
exercises.explanation: An aggregation summarises matching documents. A terms aggregation groups documents by a keyword value.

exercises.question: What does this update change?
exercises.explanation: The update API can change selected fields of an existing document. Its doc object describes the partial change.

exercises.question: What keeps this delete limited to one record?
exercises.explanation: The delete API removes one document by its id. Its scope is much narrower than deleting a whole index.
